case.summary: Transaction 3478561 for $74.96 was flagged as part of a coordinated fraud ring using a specific device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M) across 28 unrelated cardholders within one month, all appearing as new devices behind an anonymous proxy. The graph evidence shows this device was used by 52 cards dataset-wide but concentrated in a one-month window affecting multiple cardholders, indicating organized abuse rather than a single account compromise. Six similar prior closed cases retrieved from memory were all confirmed fraud, five matching the undocumented pattern and two matching the shared device and region. The flagged cardholder's baseline activity of 85 transactions across two regions over six months appears legitimate, making this single online transaction an anomaly consistent with account exploitation. No additional evidence was requested. We conclude this is fraud with high confidence (0.90), part of a larger coordinated scheme, with exposure limited to $74.96 on this card.

sar.narrative: Customer C13487 holds card C13487-K1, which on November 22, 2016 at 16:11:00 UTC was used to make a $74.96 online purchase of product code C in billing region 191.0. The transaction originated from device profile SM-G935F Build/NRD90M running Android 7.0 and Chrome 62.0 for Android at 1920x1080 resolution, a device marked as new to this account and accessed through an anonymous proxy. Investigation revealed that this specific device profile was used within a single month by 28 different cardholders, each appearing as a new device on their respective accounts, all behind the same anonymous proxy infrastructure. The cardholder's baseline activity shows 85 transactions spread across 2 billing regions and both in-person and online channels between July and December 2016, with a median transaction size of $48.03. This pattern of a single concrete device build appearing as new across dozens of unrelated accounts within a short timeframe, combined with anonymous proxy masking and the absence of any legitimate shared-device scenario, indicates coordinated fraud originating from a single source rather than compromise of individual cardholders. Prior closed cases involving the same device profile yielded 8 confirmed fraud cases with no false alarms, including multiple instances flagged as undocumented patterns. The flagged transaction itself carries a total suspicious amount of $74.96. The bank blocked card C13487-K1, created a case file, flagged 28 connected cards for monitoring, escalated to analyst review, and filed a report for regulatory attention.
